title: Wide-field view of the Meathook galaxy
caption: The Meathook Galaxy, NGC 2442, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope
celestial: NGC 2442 · constellation Volans · about 55 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This wide view takes in the whole of the Meathook Galaxy, NGC 2442, together with the sky around it. Its two spiral arms are clearly lopsided, and the longer one glows pink with intense star formation. It was taken with the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope's Wide Field Imager, at La Silla in Chile.

Young stars pour out radiation that strips electrons from atoms in the gas they formed from, a process called ionization, and the energized gas then glows. So the pink patches mark where new stars have recently switched on.

Astronomers think both its lopsided shape and its burst of star formation were caused by tidal forces during a close pass by another galaxy sometime in the past. The gravity of a passing neighbor can distort a galaxy's arms and squeeze its gas into making stars.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (26.81 x 22.55 arcminutes) and distance (55 million light years), the frame spans roughly 429,000 × 361,000 light-years. Its light set out about 55 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light image was made with the Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope, with filters including one that isolates the red glow of hydrogen. The source does not publish the color mapping.
understand.eye: Long exposures collect far more light than the eye, which could never pick out the faint pink glow of star-forming gas in this galaxy.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: This ground-based picture covers far more sky than a Hubble image of the same galaxy, although it shows less fine detail. NGC 2442 lies about 55 million light-years away in the southern constellation Volans.
alt: A lopsided spiral galaxy with two uneven arms, the longer arm glowing pink, set among surrounding stars.
